article.articleSummary:
- Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed 5,904 people out of 12,021 laboratory-confirmed cases, as of 27 November 2026. The outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain. It was declared in mid-May in the northeastern Ituri province and has since spread to eight of the DRC's 26 provinces. Government data show sustained transmission across multiple regions, with response teams continuing containment, surveillance, and patient care efforts to curb the outbreak. No details on infection sources or imported/exported cases are provided in the report.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue in Cambodia: Could AI give earlier warning?
article.articleSummary: Cambodia recorded 28,074 dengue cases and 38 deaths as of July 12, 2026, up 58.1% from the same period in 2025, with climate change accelerating mosquito and virus development and rainfall creating new larval habitats. Cambodia currently lacks an operational AI dengue forecast system; Laos is piloting climate-based early warning within DHIS2, offering a potential template for Cambodia.

article.articleHeadline: Dual Hepatitis B and HIV Functional Cure Requires Dedicated Coinfected
article.articleSummary: Global HBV/HIV-1 coinfection affects about 3.4 million people among roughly 40.8 million living with HIV-1 at end-2024, with HIV-positive individuals showing 8.4% HBsAg positivity. Regional variation is substantial: West/Central Africa 12.4%, Asia-Pacific 9.8%, Latin America 5.1%, and Western Europe/North America 6.0%. Nigeria, Ghana, and Ethiopia report 10–15% coinfection; China’s registry shows 8.7% of 33,861 patients. Coinfection accelerates liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma risk: HCC incidence ~1.8 per 1,000 person-years in North America and 1.7 in Swiss cohorts. Key risk factors include age >40, HCV coinfection, alcohol, HIV viremia >500 copies/mL, HBV >200 IU/mL, low CD4 counts, and cirrhosis. Tenofovir-containing ART reduces HCC incidence, but longer survival raises lifetime risk. Functional cure requires HBV seroclearance of HBsAg for ≥24 weeks with undetectable HBV DNA and durable HIV control after stopping therapy. HBV and HIV persistence in hepatic reservoirs—HBV cccDNA and HIV in hepatocytes, Kupffer cells, and liver CD4 T cells—complicates cure.

article.articleSummary: China, a 43-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus on long-term immunosuppression developed influenza A-associated ARDS with refractory hypoxemia and septic shock, accompanied by pancytopenia and coagulopathy. article.articleHeadline: Temporal molecular features of hepatic injury in mice infected with Echinococcus multilocularis revealed by DIA-based quantitative proteomics
article.articleSummary: Alveolar echinococcosis (AE) caused by Echinococcus multilocularis induces progressive hepatic injury in a mouse model. In C57BL/6 mice, livers were collected at 1, 3 and 6 months post-infection. Histology showed early mild hepatocellular edema, middle-stage inflammatory cell–encapsulated metacestode vesicles, and late-stage extensive fibrotic remodeling. DIA-based quantitative proteomics identified 8537 proteins, with 1140 differentially expressed and 75 persistently altered across stages. Early infection featured cytochrome P450–mediated metabolic stress and mitochondrial dysfunction; the middle stage marked a transition with Ahr/JAK-STAT signaling linked to immune imbalance and incipient fibrogenesis; the late stage corresponded to sustained inflammation and extracellular matrix remodeling. Core proteins Ahr, Thy1, Rtn4 and Prlr displayed stage-specific patterns, with Thy1 increasing throughout and Ahr/Rtn4/Prlr peaking around month 3. The authors propose a triphasic injury model and provide a hepatic proteomic atlas to monitor progression and identify therapeutic targets, based in Xinjiang, China.

article.articleHeadline: Beware! Respiratory Syncytial Virus Strikes! Please keep this parent caregiving guide.
article.articleSummary: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) infections in infants are the focus of a caregiving guide from Shanghai Longhua Hospital’s pediatrics chief, Dr. Jiang Yonghong, on a Xuhui District health program. The guide outlines a four-stage RSV illness: days 1–3 early with runny nose, nasal congestion, and cough; days 3–5 with worsening cough, breathlessness, wheeze, fever, and poor feeding; days 5–7 recovery as fever declines; 2–4 weeks post-infection cough and phlegm may persist. There is no specific antiviral; treatment is supportive. If oxygen is needed, provide oxygen; wheezing managed with inhaled corticosteroids and bronchodilators; severe cases may require IV steroids. Home care includes elevating the head of the bed 15–30°, saline nasal spray with gentle suction, small frequent feeds, and a quiet environment; avoid indoor smoking and irritants. Maintain 20–24°C and 50–70% humidity; use a humidifier with clean water and no additives; nebulization requires medical evaluation to avoid delays in care.

article.articleHeadline: Time Series Models Track Monthly Tuberculosis and HIV Coinfection
article.articleSummary: Monthly tuberculosis and HIV coinfection registrations in Sichuan, China (9,012 patients across 132 months from January 2015 to December 2025) were analyzed to forecast short-term volumes with seasonal ARIMA (SARIMA) models. Across 134 specifications, SARIMA(0,1,1)(1,0,1)[12] without drift emerged as optimal by corrected AIC on the full series, though several structures yielded similar information criteria. An independent validation using data through December 2022 identified SARIMA(0,1,1)(1,0,0)[12], which was tested with a 36-month fixed-origin holdout and expanding-window forecasts for 2023–2025 against naive baselines. One-step RMSE reached 17.20 vs 18.74 naive and 25.38 seasonal naive; twelve-month RMSE was 26.30, with MAE worse than seasonal naive. Prediction interval coverage was underwhelming (80% PI 77.8%, 95% PI 88.9%). A five-month holdout for Jan–May 2026 yielded RMSE 12.22 but May counts exceeded estimates, falling below the 80% PI. Annual coinfection registrations declined 10.2% from 2024 to 2025. Surveillance counts reflect reporting dynamics rather than true incidence, limiting transferability.

article.articleHeadline: Machine Learning Models Predict Relative COVID-19 Wave Sizes Using Genomic
article.articleSummary: Global modeling study shows machine learning can forecast the relative peak size of emerging SARS-CoV-2 waves using early growth data. Analyzing 43 countries, researchers built random-forest regression models to determine whether a new variant would produce a larger or smaller weekly peak than the preceding dominant variant. Focusing on Delta→Omicron BA.1 and BA.1→BA.2 transitions, combining viral genomic metrics with demographic, mobility, policy, and seroprevalence indicators, the approach correctly identified wave directionality in up to 91% of jurisdictions. Data sources include JHU CSSE, WHO, Oxford COVID-19 Government Response Tracker, SeroTracker, Google Mobility, Our World in Data, and GISAID sequences filtered by Nextclade against Wuhan-Hu-1. Inclusion required at least 10 sequences per week (June 2021–June 2022). Time zero marks when a variant reaches 10% weekly sequences, with a five-week observation window, and leave-one-country-out cross-validation using ensembles of up to 100k trees.

article.articleHeadline: New Blood Protein Test Could Help Doctors Track COVID-19, Flu Recovery And Other Viral Infections: Lancet
article.articleSummary: Beijing outpatient clinic study enrolled 201 adults with respiratory viral infections from December 2023 to March 2024; 59 influenza A, 43 influenza B, 78 SARS-CoV-2, 21 other viruses. Blood myxovirus resistance protein A (MxA) levels, measured by fluorescence-based assay, were high at symptom onset (median 116 ng/mL), peaking around day 2 and decreasing to below 50 ng/mL by day 10. MxA dynamics correlated with viral reads via sequencing and with systemic/respiratory symptom scores, strongest early in infection. Virus-specific patterns: MxA declined faster with SARS-CoV-2 than influenza; among influenza B, declines were faster with baloxavir than oseltamivir. Not a stand-alone recovery test; MxA declined more slowly than viral load, and a low value does not confirm non-infectiousness. An exploratory finding: higher baseline MxA associated with in-hospital mortality in 48 hospitalized patients with lower respiratory infections and fever. Limitations: single hospital, limited follow-up, excluded immunosuppressed; requires larger validation.

article.articleHeadline: Food allergies on the rise: more reports in Italy.
article.articleSummary: RASFF 2025 shows rising food alerts; total notifications 5,206, down slightly from 2024. Border rejections 1,401 (-16.1%), alerts 1,415 (+10.4%), about 27.2% of notices. Pesticides like chlorpyrifos and chlorpyrifos-methyl are frequently detected. Top food groups: fruits and vegetables (1,033), dried fruits and seeds (649), dietary supplements (409); confectionery notices rose. Italy sent 485 notifications to RASFF, with 226 for products of Italian origin. Most notices concern Turkish origin products (477), followed by China (327) and the Netherlands (323). Nationally: 349 alerts (+~15%), with about 85% serious or potentially serious. Notable outbreaks: Calabria and Sardinia botulism clusters in summer 2025; Listeria monocytogenes ST451 cluster (48 cases, 3 deaths) linked to salumi/sausages but no single source proven. Regions with most national notifications: Lazio, Lombardy, Veneto; main origins: Veneto, Emilia-Romagna, Lombardy. Calls for stronger supplier controls.

article.articleHeadline: Large Bronchial Cast Removed from Infant with Parainfluenza Virus Pneumonia
article.articleSummary: Massive plastic bronchitis temporally linked to human parainfluenza virus type 3 (HPIV-3) pneumonia in an 11-month-old infant in Shanghai, China. Case from Shanghai Children's Hospital and Shanghai Sixth People's Hospital describes bilateral pulmonary infiltrates on chest radiography with left-lower-lobe consolidation on CT. Flexible bronchoscopy removed a single branching cast about 45 mm long obstructing the left main bronchus to the left lower lobe, following saline lavage. Pathology and molecular analyses of the cast and bronchoalveolar lavage identified HPIV-3 (65,790 t-NGS reads) with co-detection of Streptococcus mitis and Klebsiella pneumoniae; histology showed inflammatory infiltrates with PAS-positive material, consistent with Type I inflammatory plastic bronchitis. Treatment included amoxicillin-clavulanate, systemic methylprednisolone, and nebulized budesonide with ipratropium and salbutamol, with complete clinical recovery and radiographic resolution within one week. The report underscores prompt bronchoscopy for cast removal in HPIV-3–associated cases.

article.articleHeadline: Authorities step up anti-dengue operations in Luyang residential area
article.articleSummary: Dengue in Luyang, Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, prompted authorities to designate Taman Austral Park as high risk and launch house-to-house inspections in November. UPPM Luyang, led by Simon Chin, with the Kota Kinabalu Health Office and DBKK, carried out joint checks at homes and nearby construction sites. The Health Office conducted fogging and applied larvicides to curb Aedes populations. Inspectors checked for stagnant water and educated residents on Aedes breeding and dengue prevention. Daytime-active Aedes mosquitoes—black-and-white—breed in small water sources such as bottle caps, flowerpot saucers, discarded containers and roof gutters; their eggs resist drying for months and hatch when water returns. Residents were urged to spend 10 minutes weekly removing standing water, cover storage containers, clear drains, dispose of water-collecting refuse, and seek prompt medical care for fever, headaches, pain behind the eyes, muscle aches or rashes. Fogging targets adults; source reduction and ongoing monitoring remain essential.

article.articleHeadline: Bird Migration: How Large Is the Epidemiological Risk?
article.articleSummary: As of 26 November 2026, autumn wild bird migration raises infectious disease concerns for poultry. While migratory waterfowl can carry avian influenza virus, risk to poultry farms cannot be attributed solely to migrating birds. Avian influenza viruses exist as low-pathogenic (LPAI) and high-pathogenic (HPAI) lineages. LPAI infections in birds are often mild or asymptomatic; HPAI can cause rapid disease progression with massive mortality in domestic poultry, notably turkeys and chickens. The influenza virus is highly mutable, with genetic reassortment potentially altering pathogenicity, virulence, and host range. Migratory birds can introduce the virus, but farm introduction and spread have multiple routes beyond wild birds. Since 1959, Scotland first isolated an HPAI strain; in 1997 Hong Kong reported the first human infections and deaths, though sustained human-to-human transmission has not been observed. High-density poultry farms warrant strict biosecurity; ongoing surveillance and modeling are essential.

article.articleHeadline: Clinicians Advised to Reopen Tuberculosis Differential During Complex CAR T
article.articleSummary: Active Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can masquerade as common post–infusion syndromes in CAR-T recipients, creating a diagnostic dilemma when patients develop unexplained fever or new pulmonary findings after infusion. TB risk in CAR-T patients reflects cumulative prior therapies and host vulnerabilities—cytopenias, lymphodepletion, steroids, hypogammaglobulinemia, and delayed immune reconstitution—rather than the infused product itself. The commentary emphasizes targeted, not automated, second-pass evaluation to reopen evolving differential diagnoses. Direct clinical evidence is limited: a 2023 single-center retrospective of 427 CD19/CD22 CAR-T recipients identified five microbiologically confirmed TB cases (23 days to 11 months post-infusion) with pulmonary, CNS, pleural, osseous, lymph node, and soft-tissue disease. A 2026 Brazilian cohort noted one TB episode among 23 CD19 CAR recipients; a peri-infusion report described active pulmonary TB diagnosed before infusion, with CAR-T proceeding after 11 weeks of anti-TB therapy. Guidelines advocate rigorous pre-treatment infectious screening and risk-adapted evaluation.

article.articleHeadline: HIV Incidence Remains Consistently High Among Rio MSM and Transgender Women
article.articleSummary: HIV incidence remains consistently high among men who have sex with men (MSM) and transgender women at a major referral center in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, from 2018–2023. Among 8,103 adults tested, 937 HIV-positive (seropositivity 11.6%); stored samples from 810 were AVIDITY-tested, with 193 (23.8%) recent infections. Estimated overall annualized incidence: 5.32% (95% CI 4.03–6.60%), higher in MSM at 5.56% (95% CI 4.17–6.94%) and transgender women at 4.33% (95% CI 2.59–6.07%). Linear trend analysis showed a non-significant negative average annual percent change for MSM (−7.7%/yr, p=0.058) and transgender women (−8.1%/yr, p=0.328). Breakpoint tests with a 2020 breakpoint did not significantly improve fit (MSM p=0.159; TW p=0.192). Authors conclude incidence remains unacceptably high, requiring intensified, targeted prevention for these key populations in Rio de Janeiro.

article.articleHeadline: Faith leaders unite to end tuberculosis
article.articleSummary: At the Union World Conference on Lung Health in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on 19 November, the World Council of Churches (WCC), Stop TB Partnership and Stop TB Brasil hosted Faith, Compassion, and Collective Action: Religious Leaders United to End TB. The dialogue drew religious leaders with decades of TB experience, young advocates, and Indigenous leaders, exploring how faith communities can influence TB responses. They identified stigma, myths, and social determinants—poverty, gender inequality, HIV—as major barriers, and stressed that TB is not solely a medical issue. They urged demystification within congregations, increased awareness among faith leaders and traditional healers, and sustained political commitment. Practical support proposed includes nutritional/food assistance, financial aid for vulnerable families, and transportation to services, with emphasis on continuing support after treatment to address long-term consequences.

article.articleHeadline: Health: Digital Radar for Outbreak Detection Already Exists in Brazil
article.articleSummary: ÆSOP (Digital Surtos Radar) is Brazil’s national early alert system for outbreaks, developed by Fiocruz, UFRJ and the Health Ministry. It combines about 7 million weekly SUS attendances with over-the-counter drug sales data from pharmacies to monitor all 5,571 municipalities (188 million people). It serves as an early warning for respiratory illnesses and arboviruses such as dengue and chikungunya, signaling increases one to four weeks before they reach hospitals. In Amazonas during the 2024 Parintins festival (≈130,000 visitors), alerts appeared three weeks prior, enabling local action. In dengue, primary care alerts anticipated about 80% of outbreaks in medium/large municipalities. The system also helps identify likely pathogens and spread patterns. Implemented since 2022, it is used by 24 states, with nationwide expansion and Rockefeller Foundation support, and provides dashboards to health authorities without replacing frontline work.

The complete list of municipalities was not released; Botucatu and nearby towns cannot be confirmed due to data gaps. Health authorities emphasize ongoing surveillance and transparent reporting.

article.articleHeadline: Captive Wild Boars in Brazil Harbor Highly Multidrug-Resistant Escherichia
article.articleSummary: In Goiás State, Brazil, captive European wild boars (Sus scrofa scrofa) on two licensed farms showed a 56.0% carriage of Escherichia coli and 1.0% carriage of Salmonella enterica. From 100 rectal swabs of clinically healthy boars collected Sept 2014–Feb 2017, 98.2% of E. coli isolates were resistant to four or more antimicrobial classes, with every isolate having a multiple antimicrobial resistance index >0.2. A single Salmonella enterica isolate, serotype O:6,8, was resistant to ampicillin, amoxicillin, and sulfonamides but susceptible to third-generation cephalosporins, and showed no targeted virulence or resistance genes molecularly. Antimicrobial susceptibility used disk diffusion per CLSI M100 guidelines across nine antibiotics; MDR defined as resistance to three or more classes. The study highlights invasive wild boar expansion in Brazilian biomes and their role as wildlife reservoirs for zoonoses (e.g., Leptospira, Toxoplasma, Brucella, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, hepatitis E), raising concerns about bidirectional pathogen exchange at the human–livestock–wildlife interface amid increasing hybridization with domestic swine.

A dengue-related fetal death in Chimbote was reported; the newborn remains hospitalized.

article.articleHeadline: Oropouche Virus Surveillance Highlights Expanding Urban Outbreaks and
article.articleSummary: Oropouche virus has escalated into an urgent public health concern after a late-2023 epidemiological shift. First identified in Trinidad (1955), it historically caused outbreaks in forested Amazonian Brazil and neighboring nations. In 2024, >11,600 laboratory-confirmed infections were recorded across the Americas; by 30 April 2025, 11,634 confirmed human cases and two deaths across ten countries and one territory (Brazil, Bolivia, Peru, Colombia, Cuba, Ecuador, Guyana, Panama, among others). Brazil reported 3,678 cases Jan–Apr 2025; female predominance 51.8%. Travel-associated imported cases occurred in Canada, the United States, and several European countries. Underdiagnosis likely underestimates true incidence due to rural diagnostics and overlap with dengue, chikungunya, Zika. Urban transmission is driven by Culicoides paraensis; sylvatic cycle incompletely characterized. The segmented genome (S, M, L) enables reassortment (Perdões, Madre de Dios, Iquitos), challenging immunity and vaccines. Infection begins after midges bite, with replication in macrophages, endothelial, and epithelial cells.

triage.triage_reason: オロプーシュウイルスが都市部へ拡大し、複数国（ブラジルを含む南米諸国）で確認例・渡航関連症例が報告されており、IHR基準の『異常性』『国際的拡大リスク』の2つに該当するためフルリスク評価に進む。
triage.notes: 記事は南米全域（ブラジル、ボリビア、ペルー、コロンビア、キューバ、エクアドル、ガイアナ、パナマ等）での流行を扱う総説記事だが、対象国リストに含まれるのはブラジルのみ。ペルー・ボリビア等対象国リスト外は除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Flesh-eating bacteria kill in the U.S.; is there a risk on Brazilian beaches?
article.articleSummary: Vibrio vulnificus, the flesh-eating bacteria, caused seven deaths in Florida this year, with 36 cases reported through November 24, 2026. The organism naturally inhabits coastal and brackish waters and thrives in higher temperatures; severe infections destroy skin tissue and may require amputation. Transmission mainly occurs via raw or undercooked oysters and shellfish, but wounds exposed to seawater can also become infected, causing pain, redness, swelling and blisters. Ingestion may cause diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting. High-risk groups include chronic liver disease, diabetes and immunocompromised individuals; CDC estimates about 20% mortality, with some cases advancing within 1–2 days. Prevention: avoid raw shellfish; avoid entering the sea with open wounds; wear protective footwear; promptly clean wounds. In Brazil, a 2025 study in Laguna, Santa Catarina found Vibrio species in oysters and mussels; V. vulnificus appeared in three samples in summer. No recent Brazilian alerts, but guidance applies for at-risk groups.

article.articleHeadline: Mpox concerns return in Brazil after a rise in cases; see what is known about the outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) concerns have resurfaced in Brazil, with 1,499 diagnoses in 2026 to date, a 39.4% rise from 1,075 in all of 2025. In São Paulo, 120 cases were reported by Nov 24, up from 81 in October and 22 in September, signaling intensified activity but well below the 2022 peak when Brazil recorded 10,591 cases. Experts attribute the rise to a mix of factors: after the 2022 outbreak risk perception declined even as the virus continued circulating (1,989 cases in 2024). Ongoing transmission chains, a large pool of susceptible individuals, limited vaccination coverage, and diagnostic challenges—all with some lesions being discreet—may fuel increases. Virologist Clarissa Damaso (UFRJ) says a single cause cannot be determined; crowded events and close contact likely facilitate transmission, but evidence for a specific trigger remains lacking.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルで症例増加によりMpox(サル痘)への懸念が再燃、流行の現状について
triage.triage_reason: WPRO基準で複数該当（持続的曝露・流行しやすさ・異常増加）があり、記事自体が社会的関心の再燃を報じているため。
triage.notes: 2022年のピーク（10,591例）と比較すると現状は規模が小さいが、2026年の症例数が前年比39.4%増加しており、持続的な感染伝播とワクチン接種率の低さが懸念材料として指摘されている。重症度・死亡例の記載はなし。

article.articleHeadline: Jardim Eldorado receives a cleanup drive, dengue control, and services for the residents of Cordeirópolis - Portal Veloz
article.articleSummary: Jardim Eldorado, in Cordeirópolis, launches Prefeitura Presente, a multi-secretariat effort to bring public services, environmental cleanup, health, education, and citizenship initiatives directly to neighborhoods. The first phase runs 27–28 November, starting with a Cata-Treco waste collection to remove items that can collect water and breed Aedes aegypti; residents should place materials outside their homes the evening before. On 28 November, the Day D against dengue occurs from 8:00 to 11:00, with awareness and prevention work by municipal staff alongside health agents; the Jardim Eldorado Health Post will offer various services. Escola Municipal Geraldo Rocha hosts environmental education activities, obstacle-by-breeding-site exchanges for prizes, PET bottle collection, reading corner, children’s workshops, cultural activities, and student project exhibits. If it rains, house visits are suspended. A second phase is scheduled for 5 December, 8:00–11:00, at the same school with public input, animal sterilization/microchip registration, and Cadastro Único guidance at CRAS Eldorado.

triage.triage_reason: 単一自治体での定例的なデング予防啓発・清掃活動に関する内容であり、症例数や異常な流行状況の報告はなく、公衆衛生上の重大性や社会的関心の高まりを示す情報もない。
triage.notes: 記事はブラジル・サンパウロ州コルデイロポリス市における予防的な清掃・啓発イベントの告知であり、デング熱の発生状況や症例数についての記載はない。対象国リストにBrazilは含まれるが、本記事の主題は地域イベントの告知であり、感染症アウトブレイクの報告ではないため、トリアージ対象としての重要性は低いと判断した。

article.articleHeadline: After visiting the 'ET Bilu' community, actress Rosa Marya is hospitalized with leishmaniasis.
article.articleSummary: Actress Rosa Marya Colin, known for playing Tia Nastácia in the 2007 Sítio do Picapau Amarelo, is hospitalized at Humap-UFMS to treat leishmaniasis. She had been visiting the Zigurats community in Corguinho, Mato Grosso do Sul, where the ET Bilu story gained notoriety, and stayed about a week before symptoms began. As of November 26, 2026, she remains in hospital receiving medications and antibiotics; doctors expect another week of treatment. Leishmaniasis is transmitted by female sandflies; skin ulcers are common, with possible internal organ involvement in severe cases. The SUS provides free medicines for all forms, and early treatment leads to cure. Local authorities report concerns about outsiders arriving infected and transmission to residents near vegetation. Fumigation was not authorized by the state due to habitat and potential impacts on bees. Suspected cases also in Furnas da Boa Sorte, Assentamento Vista Alegre, and other rural Corguinho areas.

triage.triage_reason: 単一の著名人症例であり地域的な流行拡大の明確な証拠はないが、同地域での疑い例複数報告や媒介昆虫対策の懸念があり経過観察が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: Dengue fever overwhelms Vilhena's urgent care unit with nearly 750 patient visits in a single day.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever overwhelms Vilhena's urgent care unit with nearly 750 visits in a single day. In Vilhena, Rondônia, Brazil, authorities treat the dengue situation as an epidemic, placing heavy pressure on the public health system. On 25 November 2026, the Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) logged about 750 attendances between 7:00 and midnight, underscoring the outbreak's severity. The report emphasizes the importance of residents recognizing dengue symptoms and following health team guidance. The municipality continues to strain public services, and the article does not report any deaths. This outbreak highlights dengue as an epidemic in Vilhena, signaling the need for vigilance, prevention measures, and timely care for suspected cases.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱がビリェーナの救急医療施設を圧迫、1日で約750件の受診
triage.triage_reason: 地域レベルでの医療逼迫は見られるが、死亡例の報告はなく、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクも不明であるため、続報を注視する段階と判断。
triage.notes: ブラジルではデング熱は季節的に頻発する疾患であり、本件は地域（ロンドニア州ビリェーナ市）レベルでの医療逼迫を報じるもの。死亡報告はなく、国際的な公衆衛生上の脅威としての性質は現時点で低いと考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: Rise in COVID-19 cases drives demand for self-tests, and pharmacies run out of stock in Uberaba
article.articleSummary: Rising COVID-19 activity in Uberaba, Brazil, drives demand for self-testing with pharmacies reporting stockouts and price variation (R$34-R$54.90). Public health data show 101 new confirmed cases in Uberaba from Nov 15–21, up from 47 the previous week, based on 288 public tests with 93 positives; influenza-like illness syndromic visits increased from 390 to 529. Autotests are antigen-based, yield 15–30 minutes, and can be self-administered, most reliable in days 2–5 of symptoms. Negative results may be false negatives; symptomatic individuals should seek health care and consider retesting. Positive results indicate probable infection; high-risk groups (elderly, pregnant, immunocompromised, chronic disease) should obtain guidance. Importantly, stock availability varies by store; some expect replenishment within a week, others have already placed orders with 1–2 day delivery estimates. Emphasis on testing timing (3rd–5th day) and urgent symptoms require emergency care.

triage.headline_ja: COVID-19感染者数の増加により自己検査キットの需要が増加、ウベラバの薬局で在庫切れ
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル国内一都市における季節性のCOVID-19/インフルエンザ様疾患の増加であり、通常の季節変動の範囲内で国際的な拡大リスクや異常性は認められない。
triage.notes: 地元での検査需要増加・在庫不足に関する生活情報記事であり、公衆衛生上の緊急事態を示す内容ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Chickenpox among prisoners in Alappuzha district jail; new inmates will not be admitted.
article.articleSummary: Chickenpox outbreak at Alappuzha district jail in Kerala leads to a halt on admitting new inmates. Sixteen inmates were initially infected, with the first case reported on October 15; eight more were later confirmed, including a healthcare worker. By month’s end, 24 prisoners had contracted the disease. Infected individuals were moved to a dedicated isolation cell, and preventive immunization or prophylaxis was administered to others to curb transmission. The Health Department notes poor ventilation and severe overcrowding: the district jail, designed for 84, currently houses 126 inmates, with some cells holding up to 12 people. Human rights concerns have been raised regarding conditions. Prisoners will be relocated to sub-jails or other jails; if sub-jails fill, transfers to the Central Jail will follow. Similar overcrowding issues exist in other state jails. 26 November 2026.

triage.headline_ja: アラップーザ県刑務所で水痘発生、新規収監者の受け入れを停止
triage.triage_reason: 刑務所内という閉鎖・過密環境での水痘集団発生で、感染拡大リスクはあるが国際的な公衆衛生上の深刻性や渡航貿易制限には該当せず、限定的な地域事案として続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 水痘は一般的にワクチン予防可能で致死率も低い疾患。過密状態の刑務所という特殊環境での集団発生であり、人権上の懸念はあるが公衆衛生上の国際的影響は限定的。

article.articleHeadline: Avian influenza in Tamil Nadu upends the egg market; prices fall by as much as 20% in eight days; with exports halted, eggs pile up in the domestic market; feed costs rise by 50%.
article.articleSummary: Avian influenza was confirmed in Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu, on November 13, prompting culling in affected zones and a 90-day poultry farming ban; exports paused, driving a domestic egg glut. Namakkal, the hub handling over 90% of India’s egg exports, faced export stoppage, and egg prices fell from 6.70 to 5.60 rupees per egg by November 11 (about 19%). Across the south, prices dropped by more than 15%; Delhi, West Bengal, Gujarat, Maharashtra saw 6–10% declines. Last year Namakkal shipped about 1 crore eggs daily. Rising feed costs—corn up ~50%, soybean ~30%, plus peanut meal and other feeds—pressured farmers even before the outbreak. With feed shortages and subdued demand, egg and poultry production remain unprofitable: producing 1 kg of chicken costs over Rs 120, while market price hovers around Rs 80 (roughly Rs 40 loss). Officials urge urgent intervention until exports resume and domestic demand rebounds.

triage.notes: 記事はタミルナードゥ州（クダロール、ナーマッカル）での家禽の鳥インフルエンザ発生に伴う卵市場・輸出への経済的影響を主題としており、人の感染例は言及されていない。デリー、西ベンガル、グジャラート、マハラシュトラは価格下落の影響地域として言及されているが、発生地ではなく市場影響地のため、verified_locationsにはインド（国全体）のみを計上した。

article.articleHeadline: 120 dengue patients in 55 days! In Varanasi, the rate has tripled, and platelet demand has also doubled.
article.articleSummary: Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, India is experiencing a dengue fever surge. As of 26 November 2026, the district reports a total of 176 dengue cases (126 urban, 50 rural). July–September saw 56 cases; October–November added 120 cases in 55 days, signaling a rapid rise in transmission, with urban areas more affected. Hotspot areas are being sprayed regularly, larval surveys conducted, and vector-control efforts intensified, including fogging at 282 sites between 1 September and 22 November. Seventeen wards have been identified for targeted intervention, with cleaning and debris-removal to curb mosquito breeding. Platelet demand has risen alongside cases; medical facilities (IMA and BHU blood banks) report requests for 10+ platelets, up from 5–7 two months earlier. Authorities stress sustained surveillance and public health actions to contain dengue.

triage.headline_ja: 55日間でデング熱患者120人！バラナシでは感染率が3倍に、血小板の需要も倍増
triage.triage_reason: インド・バラナシ県での季節性デング熱の増加が報告されているが、地域内での対応（防疫・血小板供給）が進んでおり、国際的拡大や渡航制限につながる兆候は見られないため、続報を注視する段階と判断。
triage.notes: デング熱はインドで季節的に流行する既知の感染症であり、今回の報告は地域的な増加（ウッタル・プラデーシュ州バラナシ）に限定される。地元当局による防蚊対策・血小板供給強化が進行中であり、現時点で国際的リスクは低いと考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: Cauvery Delta Study Finds Scrub Typhus Pathogen in Rodents and Chiggers
article.articleSummary: Scrub typhus pathogen Orientia tsutsugamushi was detected by genetic analysis in both vector mites and host tissues across five landscape types in Thiruvarur district, Tamil Nadu, from September 2023 to December 2024, evidencing active local circulation in an intensively cultivated agricultural basin. Sequencing clustered with Karp-related lineages. In a field survey of 282 small mammals (193 Rattus rattus, 40 Millardia meltada, 40 Bandicota indica, 9 Suncus murinus), 134 hosts (47.5%) harbored trombiculid mites, yielding 3,747 larvae (mean infestation 13.29 larvae/host; mean intensity 27.96). Six mite taxa were found, dominated by Leptotrombidium deliense (62.9%) and L. rajasthanense (36.5%). Riverine habitats along the Vennar/Vettar had the highest infestation (71.1%), mangroves 63.2%, urban/peri-urban/paddy 41.1–43.3%. Paddy sites had the most chiggers (1,128) and highest mean intensity (49.04). Millardia meltada showed 31.85 larvae/host; Suncus murinus (nine hosts) carried 89.67 larvae/host. National surveillance reports 127 scrub typhus outbreaks (2009–2023): 3,751 human cases and 93 deaths; rural Tamil Nadu hospitalization approximates one-fifth of diagnosed cases. The study clarifies environmental distribution, transmission ecology, and reservoir associations, underscoring ongoing scrub typhus risk in rural Tamil Nadu.

triage.triage_reason: これは特定のアウトブレイク報告ではなく学術的な生態学研究であり、人間の症例急増等の即時的な公衆衛生上の脅威は示されていないが、農村タミルナドゥ州でのツツガムシ病の継続的リスクを示しており、今後の動向を注視する価値がある。
triage.notes: 本記事は2009-2023年の国家サーベイランスデータ（127件のアウトブレイク、3,751症例、93死亡）を引用した学術研究であり、現在進行中の急性アウトブレイクの報告ではない。媒介動物・宿主の生態学的分布に関する知見を提供するもので、新規の公衆衛生上の緊急事態ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Why kissing newborns can be dangerous and how parents can prevent infections
article.articleSummary: Newborns are highly vulnerable to infections in the first weeks due to immature immune systems, especially premature babies or those with health conditions. From New Delhi, the guidance warns that kissing a newborn on the face, lips or hands can transmit germs via saliva and droplets, notably herpes simplex virus which can cause serious illness in infants, and respiratory viruses like RSV and influenza. Because many infections are contagious even without symptoms, parents should set boundaries: wash hands before touching the baby, avoid kissing, limit the number and duration of visits, and ensure visitors with fever, cough, cold, sore throat, skin infections or illnesses postpone visits. For premature infants, extra precautions and adherence to the paediatrician’s guidance on vaccination, hygiene, and avoiding crowded places are advised. Seek medical care for fever ≥38°C in a baby under 3 months, poor feeding, sleepiness, breathing difficulties or changes in skin color.

article.articleHeadline: Another severe infection is ravaging Borsod County! It begins with fever, fatigue, and muscle pain.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-11-26, Hungary’s National Public Health Institute (NPHI) reported multiple infectious-disease events. In Borsod-Abaúj-Zemplén, counts include campylobacteriosis 4, salmonella 5, rotavirus 4, infectious hepatitis 21, hepatitis A 19, scarlet fever 5, chickenpox 11, and pertussis 1, with national totals for these diseases: campylobacteriosis 139, salmonella 81, rotavirus 34, infectious hepatitis 40, hepatitis A 31, scarlet fever 57, and chickenpox 57. Two gastroenteritis outbreaks were reported: Somogy county elementary school outbreak, 66 ill of 212 exposed (diarrhea, vomiting); Fejér county nursing-home outbreak, 35 ill of 140 exposed (fever, vomiting, diarrhea), one hospitalization, suspected food source. In Budapest, a lab-confirmed imported measles (morbilli) case in a 38-year-old man who had been in India during incubation and was unvaccinated. Five lab-confirmed mpox cases: four in Budapest, one in Csongrád-Csanád; ages 23–36; none vaccinated against mpox. Hepatitis types A–G are described.

triage.triage_reason: ハンガリー国内で複数の感染症（カンピロバクター症、サルモネラ、A型肝炎、水痘、百日咳など）の定期報告があり、輸入麻疹症例やmpoxクラスター（5例）も確認されたが、重症度や拡大傾向に関する情報が不足しており、現時点ではフルリスク評価には至らない。

article.articleHeadline: Young man arrested in Kolkata for concealing HIV-positive status from his partner before marriage - Punjab Kesari
article.articleSummary: As of November 26, 2026, in Kolkata's Bansdroni area, a man working at a private institution was arrested for allegedly concealing his HIV-positive status from his partner before marriage. The partner, a nurse at a private hospital, had met him on social media years earlier; they planned marriage and starting a family. She alleges he hid his infection despite knowing it, prompting trust issues when she pushed for tests. He initially refused medical testing but consented later; HIV tests confirmed his status, and she subsequently tested as well. She claims he disclosed past sexual relations with several other women. The case was filed at Bansdroni Police Station, and the man was arrested on Wednesday under multiple charges, including fraud and deception, police said.

article.articleHeadline: From pigeon droppings to crabgrass, the diseases caused by them this season could be dangerous.
article.articleSummary: Pigeon droppings and feathers in Indian urban and rural settings harbor over 20 pathogenic bacteria and fungi, potentially linked to more than 60 diseases, raising respiratory and skin risk as pigeon populations grow in cities. Dry droppings disperse dust carrying spores and antigens; feather-derived matter also disseminates allergens. In November–December, dry air and reduced ventilation indoors intensify respiratory infections, particularly among children, the elderly, asthmatics, and immunocompromised individuals. Separately, Parthenium hysterophorus, or Congress grass/Parthenium (carrot grass), is an invasive weed along roadsides, vacant plots, and fields. It contains sesquiterpene lactones (parthenin) and can irritate crops and be toxic to livestock; continuous exposure among farmers and outdoor workers poses further health risks via pollen and contact. Preventive guidance emphasizes cleanliness, reducing pigeon feeding, weed control, and consulting health professionals for persistent symptoms.

article.articleHeadline: No sign of biting winter; Poush month brings mosquitoes! Mosquito breeding even in December–January? Concerns rising due to Super El Niño.
article.articleSummary: As of 26 November 2026, Kolkata and the Gangetic South Bengal region may see extended mosquito breeding into December–January due to warmer-winter conditions linked to Super El Niño. A Center for Climatic Health survey warns dengue and malaria risks could rise as mosquitoes lay eggs and larvae in humid, damp environments even during winter. Temperatures could briefly fall below 15°C for a few days, but most of December–January may stay above that threshold, with humidity and cloudy spells from El Niño-driven low-pressure systems potentially sustaining breeding. The threat is that mosquito populations may persist beyond the usual winter lull into January. Public health guidance emphasizes removing standing water around homes, cleaning containers, using nets, and seeking prompt medical care for fever, headache, or body aches; no exact case counts are provided.

triage.headline_ja: 冬の寒さ見られず、ポウシュ月にも蚊が発生！12月〜1月も蚊の繁殖続く？スーパーエルニーニョで懸念高まる
triage.triage_reason: 具体的な症例数の報告はなく、気候要因によるデング・マラリアリスク上昇の予測記事であるため、続報を注視する段階と判断。
triage.notes: 本記事は実際の症例報告ではなく、気候変動（エルニーニョ）による蚊の繁殖期延長とデング・マラリアリスク上昇を予測した公衆衛生啓発記事。具体的な感染者数データなし。

article.articleHeadline: India Lowers Tuberculosis Incidence to 195 Cases per 100,000 People
article.articleSummary: Incidence fell to 195 per 100,000 in 2024 from 237 in 2015, but India remains the largest TB burden, contributing about 25% of cases with 2.6–2.8 million infections annually. Drug-sensitive TB treatment success exceeds 85%, yet incidence remains above the elimination threshold of fewer than one per million. Mycobacterium tuberculosis remains the leading infectious disease killer. Transmission concentrates in densely populated states—Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, West Bengal—and in overcrowded urban settlements, mining regions, tribal and peri-urban corridors; predominantly affects working-age adults 15–54, with higher case numbers in men and underreporting among women, plus persistent pediatric transmission. Undernutrition is the primary determinant; nutritional support during therapy improves survival and completion and reduces incidence among contacts. HIV and diabetes complicate control: 2.54 million people living with HIV in 2023; 2024 TB patients with documented HIV status were 2.62 million with 33,190 co-infected; co-morbid diabetes among 2.44 million tested.

article.articleHeadline: Crude Lemongrass Oil Outperforms Commercial Formulations Against Aedes
article.articleSummary: Laboratory-extracted crude essential oil from Cymbopogon citratus (lemongrass) shows markedly higher larvicidal potency and longer-lasting adult irritancy against Aedes aegypti than a commercially prepared lemongrass oil. In The Journal of Basic and Applied Zoology, the crude oil achieved a median lethal concentration (LC50) of 10.485 micrograms per milliliter against early fourth-instar larvae after 24 h, more than fourfold more effective than the commercial oil (LC50 43.504 micrograms per milliliter). The crude oil, produced by lab-scale steam distillation from lemongrass leaves collected at Dyal Singh College, New Delhi, India, displayed more chromatographic spots (seven vs fewer) and shared core terpenoid fractions such as citral, but retained additional metabolites due to minimal post-extraction processing. Adult excito-repellency tests confirmed sustained irritancy. The findings, relevant to dengue, chikungunya, Zika, and yellow fever virus transmission control, underscore how processing and chemical richness influence botanical vector management, using a laboratory Ae. aegypti strain reared from eggs.

article.articleHeadline: How to prevent the spread of mad cow disease among cattle?
article.articleSummary: Mad cow disease in cattle is caused by a skin-destroying virus, with a 4–14 day incubation. Infected animals show high fever, fatigue, lameness, swelling of forelegs and hind legs (3–5 cm lumps on the head, neck, reproductive region, and limbs), and central ulcers where the skin crusts and sloughs. Treatment involves isolating affected cows and, under veterinary guidance, addressing fever, lameness, and skin wounds. On day 1, administer a mixture of 10 g each of betel leaves, pepper, rock salt, and jaggery every 3 hours; from day 2 for 14 days, three times daily. A paste made from neem leaves, kuppaimani leaves, holy basil, maruthani leaves, turmeric powder (20 g) and garlic (10 cloves), boiled in coconut or neem oil, can be applied to ulcers. Infected cattle should be separated and not grazed. Insects may spread disease; follow veterinary advice. Calves under 6 months should be vaccinated, and vaccination should precede moving cattle by 4 weeks.

article.articleHeadline: ICMR-NIMR to bring AI and drone technology to fight malaria, with precise identification of breeding sites hidden on rooftops and in water tanks.
article.articleSummary: ICMR-NIMR is developing a semi-automated drone-based system, powered by AI, to map malaria mosquito breeding sites in dense urban India. The technology targets breeding habitats concealed on rooftops and inside water storage tanks, enabling precise, data-driven vector-control interventions in metropolitan settings. By identifying breeding hotspots via drone imagery and AI analysis, the initiative aims to guide timely larval source management and curb urban malaria transmission. This approach marks India’s push toward advanced surveillance and targeted control in crowded cities, where traditional surveys struggle to detect hidden breeding grounds in rooftops and water containers.

article.articleHeadline: Infectious diseases from free-ranging domestic animals threaten Nilgiris wildlife
article.articleSummary: Nilgiris district accounted for five of 12 wildlife deaths since 2005 likely due to infections from feral animals, per Forest Department findings to the Madras High Court. Necropsies identified canine distemper and rabies as causes across species, including leopard with canine distemper, Nilgiri langur rabies, gaur rabies, sloth bear rabies and ehrlichiosis, and golden jackal canine distemper and parvovirus. Deaths had been reported in Kodaikanal, Kalakkad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve (KMTR), Sivaganga, Theni, Kanniyakumari and Tirunelveli, with Nilgiris highest. In Gudalur, two 2026 deaths—a leopard and a tiger—were attributed to canine distemper. Officials note disease transmission from free-ranging dogs and cattle around Mudumalai Tiger Reserve; vaccination of village dogs and cattle began in Gudalur in 2026. The department plans joint vaccination across KMTR, MTR, Srivilliputhur-Megamalai TR, Sathyamangalam TR, and Anaimalai TR, with 5,766 animals vaccinated in 2026 against canine distemper, rabies, and foot-and-mouth disease. Conservationists caution numbers may undercount wildlife mortality.

article.articleHeadline: Medical officers in Tuensang trained on Ebola detection, res
article.articleSummary: One-day capacity-building training on Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) preparedness and response was conducted for medical officers and the district joint outbreak response team in Tuensang, organized by the District Surveillance Unit (DSU) and Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP) under the CMO, Tuensang, at District Hospital Tuensang. District Data Manager Langthsapila Sangtam emphasized real-time reporting via the IDSP portal. A practical session on proper PPE donning and doffing was conducted by Dr. Sharma and Dekhingridi Sangtam, BSL-2 Technician at the Integrated Molecular Diagnostics and Research Laboratory, District Hospital Tuensang.

article.articleHeadline: El Niño offers lead time -- not certainty -- against dengue in South Asia
article.articleSummary: Dengue risk in Kerala, India could be forecast by a model blending Pacific ENSO signals with local climate data (temperature, humidity, rainfall). In Kerala, about 40% of years with high modelled dengue coincide with El Niño, while roughly 57% of years with low modelled incidence align with La Niña. Pacific sea-surface temperatures correlate with Kerala cases three months ahead; including local weather can extend lead time to five months, though ENSO remains a weaker signal. A multi-variable approach—climate plus ENSO plus vector surveillance and health data—improves prediction but cannot specify outbreak start or magnitude. Such forecasts provide months for preparedness: review hotspots, circulating serotypes, diagnostics, stocks, staffing, and referral pathways. The 2023–24 El Niño coincided with the largest global dengue epidemic, Americas >90% of cases; Sri Lanka saw DENV-2 resurgence in 2025–26, raising risk, but no surge by November 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Private Providers in Bengaluru Lack Awareness of Standards for Tuberculosis
article.articleSummary: TB care standards in India (STCI) have not reached many private providers in Bengaluru, South India. A qualitative study using focus group discussions with private medical college specialists and in-depth interviews with freelancing subspecialists and general practitioners (Jan 2018–Jul 2019) found pervasive unawareness of STCI among private providers, a key component of India's TB service delivery. Barriers include a communication gap between the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP) and private practitioners, absence of dissemination platforms (such as mobile apps), and limited ground-level implementation efforts. The study underscores the need for renewed NTEP outreach to percolate standards to private providers via digital platforms and direct, one-on-one engagement in Bengaluru to improve adherence to TB care guidelines.

article.articleHeadline: Puducherry govt. intensifies dengue surveillance, preventive measures amid rising cases
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever outbreak in Puducherry UT (India) with over 1,510 cases reported through November 2026 and four deaths in recent weeks; 476 cases in November as of Nov 25, the year’s highest monthly spike. Identified hotspots include Mudaliarpet, Murungapakkam, Kosapalayam, Mettupalayam, Reddiyarpalayam, Lawspet, Gorimedu and urban areas of Villianur and Ariyankuppam. In response, the government has launched emergency measures, holding high-level meetings, intensifying fogging, anti-larval work, public campaigns, cleaning, and surveillance; implementing dry day observances in schools, source reduction, fever surveillance, and introducing larvivorous fish; Rapid Response Teams comprise medical officers, ANMs, ASHA workers, nurses, and LAD staff. Hospitals expanded fever beds (GH: 38; Medical College: 72) though bed occupancy is high. Officials urge residents to maintain clean surroundings, seek testing at government hospitals for fever, and avoid self-medication or using aspirin/ibuprofen without medical advice. Dengue symptoms include high fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, muscle/joint pain, rashes, nausea.

article.articleHeadline: Thymol and Naphthalene Repel Urban Malaria Vectors in Laboratory and
article.articleSummary: Thymol and naphthalene function as volatile spatial repellents against urban malaria vectors in India. In a spatial repellency assay with Anopheles stephensi from Jaipur, Rajasthan, at 27°C and 70% RH, both compounds reached a maximum spatial activity index of 0.675 and a median effective dose of 0.052%, outperforming oleic acid and several multi-compound blends. Molecular docking and dynamics across eleven odorant receptors and binding proteins supported a mechanism for airborne deterrence. Dose-dependent repellency occurred from 0.05% to 0.35%, tested on 1,400 female mosquitoes over two replicates, using acetone-treated emanators delivering vapour through Whatman papers. The work addresses insecticide resistance limiting indoor control; India’s malaria-prone population is around 93%, with ca. 1.5 million annual cases and Plasmodium falciparum accounting for ~40%. Spatial repellents may reduce entry into homes in India and neighboring regions.

article.articleHeadline: Treated, cured, then sick again: Why tuberculosis keeps returning to haunt patients
article.articleSummary: Recurrent pulmonary TB haunts Indian TB patients, including Navjot Singh, 42, among those relapsing after treatment at NITRD in Mehrauli and Rajan Babu Institute in GTB Nagar. Over 22 years, TB struck thrice; relapse can occur when original bacteria survive, reinfection, dormant bacilli awaken, or treatment fails. Molecular testing and drug susceptibility help detect resistance. A 2024 NLM review of 75,224 patients found recurrent TB in 2.9%; a 2026 Lancet Global Health study of 1,076 survivors in Maharashtra found 7% redeveloped TB within 12 months. India accounts for about a quarter of global TB, with 2024 estimates of 27.1 lakh new cases and over 3 lakh deaths; worldwide 10.7 million cases and 1.23 million deaths (WHO 2025 report). Many patients abandon treatment, as with Abdesh Singh in Mangolpuri who stopped after 3-4 months; poverty, crowding, malnutrition, stigma drive relapse. HIV co-infection worsens risk and requires TB diagnosis and close follow-up.

article.articleHeadline: Can a mother with hepatitis B transmit it to her child?
article.articleSummary: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection can be transmitted from mother to child, mainly during childbirth and sometimes in pregnancy. Transmission risk depends on maternal HBV DNA level and HBeAg status; with proper monitoring, treatment, and timely infant vaccination, the risk is reduced. Before pregnancy, women should be evaluated (HBsAg, HBeAg, HBV DNA, liver enzymes) to plan prevention. If HBV DNA ≥200,000 IU/mL (≈5.3 log10 IU/mL) and HBsAg positive, antiviral therapy may start around week 14 of gestation under medical supervision. At birth, all newborns should receive hepatitis B vaccine as soon as possible, ideally within 24 hours; infants of HBsAg-positive mothers should also receive HBIG within 12 hours. Infants are tested at 9–12 months for HBsAg and anti-HBs to assess infection and vaccine response. Daily caregiving is safe; breastfeeding is allowed after full prophylaxis, unless nipples are cracked or bleeding. Location: Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

article.articleHeadline: How can a meal introduce antibiotic-resistant bacteria into the body?
article.articleSummary: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria can enter the body through meals—especially undercooked meat, unwashed produce, and cross-contamination in kitchens. WHO warns that resistant bacteria can move from animals to humans along the food chain when farming, slaughtering, processing, and storage are unsafe. In livestock, antibiotics are widely used; susceptible bacteria are killed, while resistant strains survive and multiply. In Vietnam, studies find drug-resistant E. coli in chicken, pork, beef, fish, and shrimp sold in markets, with some samples carrying colistin resistance genes, last-resort antibiotic. Transmission occurs from farm to table during slaughter, transport; produce can be contaminated by polluted water or manure. Household risks include using the same knives, boards, and surfaces for raw and cooked foods, and inadequately washed vegetables. Preventive steps: cook thoroughly, separate utensils, wash hands, sanitize surfaces, and refrigerate promptly. From 2026-01-01, Vietnam plans to end antibiotic use in animal feed within defined scope. WHO notes resistance remains high.

article.articleHeadline: Rabies risk on transport routes for dogs and cats in Vietnam.
article.articleSummary: FOUR PAWS investigations reveal illegal transport of dogs and cats across Vietnam and from Laos, with trucks carrying up to 400 animals and intermediaries moving as many as 1,000 daily. Highway 1A is the trafficking artery, linking southern supply hubs to demand in Hanoi. With Vietnam recording about 70–100 human rabies deaths per year, shipments of unvaccinated animals without veterinary certificates or border checks heighten cross-border transmission risks and hinder national and regional disease controls, undermining the Zero by 30 target to end dog-mediated human rabies by 2030. Jon Rosén Bennett of Four Paws warns that each unvaccinated animal may carry deadly viruses, and highlights enforcement gaps—uneven inspections and weak interagency coordination among border control, veterinary, and regulatory bodies. Welfare concerns include overcrowding, injuries, and deaths. Calls for stronger enforcement and a nationwide ban on dog and cat meat.

article.articleHeadline: Mosquito insecticide resistance: A new challenge in dengue fever prevention and control
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever remains a major public-health challenge in Vietnam in 2026, with 170,600+ cases and 28 deaths reported through November across the country. The Aedes vectors—Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus—are increasingly resistant to common insecticides (DDT, permethrin, deltamethrin), driven by target-site mutations and metabolic mechanisms, complicating vector-control efforts. Dengue transmission now shows year-round activity and a geographic expansion from urban to rural, mountainous areas, straining local health systems. Experts advocate a shift to integrated vector management: regular insecticide susceptibility monitoring, rotating chemical classes, reducing selection pressure, researching new products, and prioritizing non-chemical measures. Larval source reduction (removing standing water) and community participation remain foundational. Southern region (Nam Bo) and Central Highlands-South Central regions face ongoing challenges. A move from pre- to post-market surveillance begins May 1, 2027, requiring firms to demonstrate safety and efficacy, with a national database and enhanced interagency information sharing to detect noncompliant products.

article.articleHeadline: Study Identifies Multidrug-Resistant MRSA in Retail Fish Imported into
article.articleSummary: MRSA (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus) identified in unprocessed retail fish imported into Germany from non-European countries. Across two sampling phases (2019–2025), 123 mecA-positive MRSA isolates were confirmed from 483 samples, primarily tropical aquaculture fish such as pangasius and tilapia. 94.3% of isolates showed resistance to at least three antimicrobial classes. Genomic typing revealed 18 sequence types, 23 spa-types, and six SCCmec architectures; dominant lineage ST188-t189-IVa comprised 41.5% (51 isolates), with ST188 overall 59.3%, ST1232 9.8%, ST1 7.3%, ST45 6.5%, and five novel STs. Most carried IVa or V cassettes, typical of community-associated lineages. 2019 Zoonoses Monitoring: 419 samples; 29.1% positive, with 81% from Vietnam. Follow-up (2024–2025) in Berlin: 64 frozen samples, 21.9% MRSA positive, all tropical-origin fish from Vietnam, India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka; temperate species negative. Implication: global seafood trade as a vehicle for resistant, virulent MRSA.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Virus Antibodies Cross-Neutralize 2026 Bundibugyo Virus Glycoprotein
article.articleSummary: Existing Ebola-virus–derived polyclonal and monoclonal antibody preparations retain cross-neutralizing activity against vesicular stomatitis virus pseudotypes bearing the surface glycoprotein of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus outbreak strain. In the context of the ongoing Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak (2026), researchers evaluated convalescent plasma from three Ebola virus disease survivors infected with Makona in Liberia (2014) and Spain (Madrid), aged 36, 44, and 45, along with equine hyperimmune plasma, murine immune serum from a mosaic GP immunogen, and therapeutic monoclonal antibodies including atoltivimab, maftivimab, odesivimab, and the Inmazeb cocktail. Equine batches LV15-0003 (2015) and MP25-0004/MP25-0005 (2025) were tested. Murine serum used a mosaic GP comprising Makona, Gulu, and Bundibugyo antigens. The 2026 Bundibugyo GP differs from 2007 by 12 amino acids. Pseudoviruses expressing these GPs and rVSV-ΔG-luc were used for neutralization assays, with the 2026 Bundibugyo sequence derived from a May 2026 Congo clinical specimen (PP_0075ZFN.1).

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Free healthcare in 14 health zones of Ituri
article.articleSummary: Free healthcare now covers 14 of Ituri province's 36 health zones during the Ebola outbreak to sustain general health services alongside the outbreak response. Presented at a 24 November 2026 technical meeting in Bunia, the measure operates under the 'direct service financing' mechanism. It addresses facility challenges such as reduced patient visits and staff departures by providing medicines, covering operating costs, and supporting human resources, with the aim of keeping clinics and hospitals functioning and ensuring continuity of care for malaria, tuberculosis, HIV, hypertension, and diabetes while Ebola response continues. Financing comes from the World Bank and the European Union. The plan was previously announced on 19 June 2026 by Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba for free care across all Ituri health facilities during the Ebola period.

article.articleHeadline: Jordan Ebola-free and a protocol for dealing with any potential infection - Sawaleef
article.articleSummary: Jordan remains Ebola-free with no infections reported. The National Center for Epidemic Control, in coordination with the Ministry of Health, WHO, and UNICEF, has an integrated protocol to manage any suspected case and prevent transmission. WHO classifies Jordan as low-risk; preventive measures have been prepared since June. Arrivals from the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda are halted, with Jordanian citizens quarantined if asymptomatic; symptomatic individuals are isolated. Uganda’s outbreak ended after two incubation periods with no new cases; Congo’s outbreak continues. The airport-to-hospital protocol covers entry screening, rapid-response teams, ambulance transfer, a designated receiving hospital, lab testing, and sample handling. Bundibugyo ebolavirus's case fatality in DRC is about 49%; transmission via body fluids, not air. Separately, Jordan intensified polio surveillance after three cases in Deir ez-Zor, Syria among unvaccinated children; two recovered, one under surveillance. Sewage testing is underway; initial environmental results are clear. Vaccination coverage exceeds 95%; vaccines are safe; the national immunization program is among the region’s most successful.

article.articleHeadline: Chinese Embassy in Malawi reminds Chinese citizens in Malawi and those planning to travel to Malawi to pay attention to the Malawi Ebola outbreak prevention measures.
article.articleSummary: Malawi’s Ebola outbreak continues with rising confirmed cases and is designated a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, signaling cross-border transmission risk. Malawi’s Ministry of Health issued travel-monitoring and prevention measures, effective immediately. The Chinese Embassy in Malawi urges Chinese citizens and travelers to observe: all entrants must complete the Traveller Health Declaration Form on arrival or beforehand; travelers from or via the Democratic Republic of Congo must self-isolate for 21 days with daily professional health monitoring; travelers from or via Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria must undergo 21 days of daily health monitoring; airports and land borders will conduct temperature checks and health screening; those with Ebola- or other infectious-disease symptoms should report to health workers or nearby medical facilities and call the Malawi public health hotline 929. All travelers, transport operators and border personnel must follow infection-prevention measures and cooperate with border officials; if contamination occurs, disinfection at entry is required. article.articleHeadline: Distinct Bat Immune Dynamics May Contribute to Resilience Against Marburg
article.articleSummary: Marburg virus, a filovirus causing severe hemorrhagic fever in humans with case fatality rates ranging from 23% to 88% across outbreaks, persists in its natural reservoir, the Egyptian fruit bat Rousettus aegyptiacus, without overt disease. Bats mount rapid, transient antiviral defenses with tightly restrained inflammatory signaling, whereas human infections trigger hyperinflammation, vascular leakage, and multi‑organ failure. Since 1967, outbreaks have occurred across sub‑Saharan Africa, beginning with laboratory exposures from Uganda-origin monkeys in Germany and Yugoslavia; major events include the Democratic Republic of the Congo (1998–2000: 154 cases, 128 deaths, 83% CFR) and Angola (2004–2005: 374 cases, 329 deaths, 88% CFR), with later reports in Equatorial Guinea, Tanzania, Ethiopia, and Rwanda (2024). In 2007, viral RNA, antibodies, and infectious virus were recovered from wild R. aegyptiacus in Gabon and Uganda, confirming the reservoir. Adult bat infection remains typically 2–5%, surging among juveniles up to 15% when maternal antibodies wane.

article.articleHeadline: New funding for response to Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the DRC, with spillover into Uganda and Kenya, has reached more than 11,700 cases and over 5,700 deaths across eight DRC provinces six months after declaration; no approved vaccine or specific treatment, with surveillance gaps and insecurity hindering containment. Four projects total €15.8 million to bolster the response: an initial €4 million from Global Health EDCTP3 and the EC, plus €11.8 million from Wellcome and the Gates Foundation. EBO-PEP 2026 (€12.8m), led by INRB and ANRS MIE, tests obeldesivir as post-exposure prophylaxis for BDBV contacts. EBONET (€1m) links networks across 23 countries to map surveillance gaps and train staff; EPoCA-BVD (€1m) develops a rugged graphene-based rapid field test; Ebola-Prep TBOX Plus (€1m) delivers practical tools for responders, including a remote molecular test, AI surveillance, a community-health-worker app and an antibody-based treatment.

article.articleHeadline: Lagos unveils disease surveillance system as 1.8 million cattle enter state annually
article.articleSummary: Lagos State unveiled the Lagos State Bioshield, a digital biosecurity framework to detect and contain emerging disease threats, amid 1.8 million cattle entering Lagos annually. With Lagos hosting about 70% of Nigeria’s international air traffic and a population of 30.1 million, authorities stress cross-sector surveillance across human, animal and environment health. The BioShield combines artificial intelligence, telemedicine and digital health surveillance in two layers: screening entrants and monitoring arrivals who develop symptoms. Health Radar uses WhatsApp, SMS and email to conduct 21-day daily health checks, linking symptomatic travellers to telemedicine, labs and referrals. Pilot at CANEX WKND covered ~19,000 delegates, including 2,298 international visitors; 2,454 telemedicine consultations; 241 clinical referrals; 219 flagged. Plans for BioShield 3.0 and Africa-wide alliance with Lagos, Cairo, Kinshasa, Johannesburg, Nairobi to harmonize preparedness. Threats include Lassa fever, dengue, yellow fever, Marburg, Ebola, and unknown pathogens.

article.articleHeadline: North Kivu: Schools and Families Mobilized to Protect Students from Ebola in Oicha - ACP.
article.articleSummary: North Kivu, Oïcha, Democratic Republic of the Congo, launches a broad mobilization to protect students from Ebola virus disease (EVD). In a two-hour public session at Saint-Esprit Parish, school officials, teachers, prefects and parents discussed making families and schools central to Ebola awareness and prevention, aiming to overcome resistance to response teams. Dr. Melcki Lukombola, head of the Ebola Treatment Center in Oïcha, urged teachers and parents to become information conduits to bridge gaps between communities and responders. Participants, including students, pressed for stronger school-based health education, timely sharing of guardians’ contact numbers with health facilities, and careful handling of forest foods and wildlife. The event, organized under the IERDC project with support from the humanitarian fund in DRC and CORACON collaboration, with Mercy Corps, International Alert, Concern Worldwide, and Viamo backing, seeks to make families and schools safe spaces for Ebola prevention.

article.articleHeadline: Likouala/Health: The prefect of the department launches the cholera vaccination campaign - Congolese Information Agency.
article.articleSummary: Cholera vaccination campaign launched in Likouala, Republic of the Congo, with Impfondo the launch site on 25 November. Prefect Jean-Pascal Koumba inaugurated the preventive campaign targeting the elderly and children aged two years and above to complement hygiene promotion and access to drinking water, amid recurrent flooding that drives transmission. Vaccination teams will go door-to-door. Since 8 August, Likouala has recorded 734 cholera cases and 38 deaths as part of the evolving outbreak, according to the departmental crisis committee on floods and cholera. The launch followed a session evaluating the epidemic and response strategies, aided by audiovisuals to illustrate epidemiology and flood-related health consequences, aimed at strengthening coordination and field responses. The Prefect praised public authorities and thanked President Denis Sassou-N'Guesso and UN agencies for addressing the department’s humanitarian emergency.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Isiro: Catholic faithful urged to apply barrier measures - ACP
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in Isiro-Niangara diocese, Haut-Uele, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, prompted Catholic leaders to urge barrier measures and hygiene practices. During the tenth anniversary of his episcopate, Bishop Dieudonné Madrapile urged parishioners to follow health authorities’ preventive messages and to protect themselves as the Ebola epidemic persists. He highlighted faith’s historic role in curbing epidemics and called Christians to maintain firm prayer while adhering to hygiene and preventive guidelines. The appeal was delivered in the Maranatha prayer room of the charismatic renewal, with Bishop Emile Mushosho of Mahagi-Nyoka present. Madrapile is also Apostolic Administrator of Isangi. The report underscores ongoing Ebola concerns in the region and the need to combine spiritual commitment with public health guidance; no case counts are provided.

article.articleHeadline: North Kivu: Assistance project for Ebola-affected families announced in Beni - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern DRC's North Kivu province (Beni): On 26 November 2026, a delegation from the Ministry of Social Affairs announced a project to assist families affected by Ebola. The plan, presented to provincial authorities in Beni, will recruit and identify social and para-social workers to deliver daily support, including food assistance and cash, within a broader recovery and social reintegration framework. Implementation starts with mobilizing personnel who will operate as community-based support workers; subsequent aid will be shaped in consultation with the identified households. The initiative is a collaboration with a partner described as reliable, mobilizing resources to provide emergency assistance and address urgent needs on the ground. The effort forms part of ongoing Ebola outbreak response efforts in the area, extending beyond immediate emergency relief to longer-term support.

article.articleHeadline: Avian Malaria Parasite in Thailand Exhibits Broad Host Plasticity and
article.articleSummary: Plasmodium collidatum, the avian malaria parasite in Thailand, shows host plasticity across pheasants, doves, pigeons, and rails yet strict geographic structuring among provinces. Five isolates collected 2018–2025 from three Thai provinces (Nakhon Sawan, Chonburi, Nakhon Pathom) were analyzed; near-complete mitochondrial genomes (~5.8 kb) revealed distinct regional lineages with zero interprovincial haplotype sharing. Infection prevalences were 2% in feral pigeons (2018), 7% in kalij pheasants and Siamese firebacks (2021), 6% in white-breasted waterhens (2023), and 5% in spotted doves (2025). Diagnoses began with nested cytb PCR, followed by mitogenomic amplification and BLAST confirmation of lineage pFANTAIL01. The results imply environmental filters, geographic distance, or local vector communities constrain dispersal more than host barriers, highlighting the value of mitogenomes for fine-scale phylogeography.

article.articleHeadline: Readily Diagnostics Builds Rapid Infection Test
article.articleSummary: Readily Diagnostics presents a rapid, multiplex molecular test platform built on padlock probes and rolling circle amplification to bridge the gap for half the world lacking basic diagnostics. The test yields visually readable results in about 25 minutes from a single kit, using gold nanoparticle-driven agglutination for a naked-eye readout. It covers nasal swabs for respiratory disease and urine or swabs for STIs. Two projects: Virca Air detects SARS CoV-two, Influenza A and B, and RSV for respiratory care, with elderly populations in mind; STI project detects Chlamydia, Gonorrhea, Trichomonas and gonorrhea AST, targeting LMICs in Africa and Asia, with home-based testing in Western markets. Gates Foundation backs STI project; collaborations in Kenya, Rwanda, Thailand; KOLs in Sweden and the US. The technology multiplexes up to 1000 padlock probes and is protected by four patents, aiming to connect central labs with point-of-care diagnostics and improve global access.

article.articleHeadline: Pilus Genes Sbp1 and Sbp3 Modulate Streptococcus Suis Virulence and
article.articleSummary: Streptococcus suis, serotype 2, sequence type 1 from Thailand (strain 26154) drives virulence via the srtBCD pilus island. Inactivation of pilus-associated genes sbp1 or sbp3 diminishes damage to human epithelial monolayers and impairs early bacterial attachment and internalization, without affecting in vitro growth. RNA profiling shows broad transcriptional down-regulation across the srtBCD locus and key virulence determinants in both mutants, with sbp1 deletion nearly abolishing transcription throughout the cluster, while sbp3 deletion yields substantial but less complete repression. Biofilm assays reveal divergent effects: Δsbp3 markedly reduces early and sustained biofilm formation; Δsbp1 reduces early biomass but accumulates more biofilm during maturation. These results indicate sbp1 and sbp3 regulate virulence beyond pilus structure, affecting CC1-associated lineages and zoonotic potential. The pathogen causes costly disease in swine and severe invasive infections in humans.

article.articleHeadline: DZIF researchers study bat viruses to better assess potential risks to humans.
article.articleSummary: West African fruit bats in Ghana and Benin harbor a bat-derived respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) variant, distinct from human RSV but in the same virus family. In 1,778 bats surveyed, 1.4% carried the virus and 9% had RSV antibodies. Genomic analysis of two bat RSVs showed they are not closely related to human RSV; however, the virus can enter human cells, albeit less efficiently than human RSV, and can dampen the innate immune response. Importantly, sera from individuals previously exposed to RSV neutralize the bat virus, and a broadly neutralizing monoclonal antibody also neutralizes it. The study emphasizes integrating genomic and functional data to assess zoonotic risk and supports development of broad-spectrum antivirals. Published in Science Advances by DZIF researchers led by Dr. Wendy Jo at Charité/ Berlin and collaborators in Hannover; next steps use reverse genetics to study pathogenesis.

article.articleHeadline: A major breakthrough in HIV prevention, a vaccine for a deadly disease has reached Africa with the aid of an Indian organization.
article.articleSummary: Lenacapavir, a long-acting HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis injection, has reached Africa via affordable generics. A first shipment of 300,000 vials arrived in Zambia, with Uganda and Zimbabwe slated to receive supplies next; Indian firm Hetero Labs Ltd is coordinating the rollout. Gilead Sciences originally developed the injection, and after favorable clinical trials in 5,000 girls and women, the WHO approved its use for HIV prevention in 2025. The two-dose-per-year regimen costs about $28,000 per person, a major access barrier. To reduce price, Gilead licensed six manufacturers for generics; Hetero Labs Ltd and Dr. Reddy Labs are among licensees, with generic prices around $40 per injection. Global Fund calls Africa shipments a major breakthrough. Sub-Saharan Africa bears a heavy HIV burden, with South Africa alone reporting about 800,000 people living with HIV; global HIV deaths last year were about 570,000. As of Nov 2026, roughly 189,000 people had received this prevention injection; 2027 targets include ten African countries and India launch plans.
